scopeDecisions.decision: Observation is through the REST surfaces (Identity Toolkit, Secure Token, Admin v2). SDK paths only where a row needs them, within AUTH-CONFIG-SDK K1 (Admin SDK for Node, Web SDK in Node).

O1: the external IdP boundary is observed with IdPs the lane controls on fireemu-oracle-idp. The OIDC id_token flow uses an issuer whose discovery document and public JWKS are deployed to the sandbox's Firebase Hosting, with ID tokens signed locally. SAML uses a locally made certificate and locally signed responses (SP-initiated). Private keys, API keys and project numbers never enter git; provider configurations and the Hosting content are deleted after each campaign. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O2: the google.com sign-in success path (a sandbox service account's generateIdToken) is out of scope; google.com is observed through its configuration and its refusals only. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O3: the OIDC code flow (returnRefreshToken, oauthRefreshToken, oauthAuthorizationCode) is deferred to a separate budgeted stage; it needs a token endpoint service on the sandbox. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

Third-party providers (facebook.com, apple.com, twitter.com, github.com, microsoft.com, yahoo.com, playgames.google.com) are out of scope for their success paths, which need real accounts; their configuration and refusals are observed. The browser behaviour of /__/auth/handler is out of scope. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O4: the strict profile verifies signed assertions of configured providers: OIDC ID tokens with keys given at startup (the auth.customTokenSigners pattern: a JWKS per issuer) and SAML responses with the provider's idpCertificates, with no network fetch from the issuer; strict refuses the unsigned fixture assertions. The emulator profile keeps the official emulator's fixture IdP and adds no refusal. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O5: verifying signed SAML XML needs XML canonicalization and XMLDSig; whether that is feasible on the sandbox is checked first, and adding a crate for it is a new owner decision at that point. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O6: tenant IdP sign-in, tenant provider configuration and blocking functions on IdP sign-in belong to AUTH-TENANT-BLOCKING (as A8, C4, K10); MFA after an IdP sign-in belongs to AUTH-MFA; Admin linkProviderUserInfo and deleteProvider are verified in AUTH-ACCOUNT. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).
Budget: US$10 per observation task, as for the other sandbox lanes. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).
Moved here: client signInWithIdp sign-in and linking (AUTH-ACCOUNT A4) and the IdP session claims (AUTH-CREDENTIAL C7).

conditions.note: Project oauthIdpConfigs create, get, list (paging), update by mask and delete: the ID rule, required members, the issuer form, the code flow and its secret, the response type, how clientSecret is returned, duplicates and missing resources.
Project inboundSamlConfigs create, get, update by mask and delete: certificate PEM validation, spConfig, signRequest and the spCertificates the service adds.
Project defaultSupportedIdpConfigs create by idpId, get, list, update by mask and delete, and defaultSupportedIdps.list. A default IdP the program writes must be absent at its start.

signInWithIdp and createAuthUri for an unconfigured, a disabled and an enabled provider (OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED, INVALID_PROVIDER_ID and the like). Strict refuses an unconfigured and a disabled provider with INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE since O4 (3ed31eb80) without a production observation; third-party-refusals steps unconfigured-oidc and disabled-oidc and provider-enablement step disabled observe the code.

A controlled OIDC IdP (O1): ID tokens signed with the run's key and published through the sandbox's Hosting; the signature, iss, aud (clientId), exp, iat, nbf, alg and kid matrix and malformed tokens. Strict refusals added by O4 (3ed31eb80) without a production observation, each answered INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE, whose code this recipe checks: a mixed-case providerId (step mixed-case-provider) and an issuer without configured keys, observed as an issuer that publishes nothing (step unpublished-issuer; production fetches discovery where fireemu reads auth.idpSigners, so a difference in the answer is a known divergence of O4, not a defect).
The nonce: absent and present, matching and not (the SHA-256 of the raw nonce in postBody).
The same ID token used twice.

A controlled SAML IdP (O1): responses signed with the run's certificate; the signature placement, Audience, Destination and Recipient, NotOnOrAfter, InResponseTo and an IdP-initiated response. Subject to the O5 feasibility check; if production takes no locally signed response, the owner is asked to move this condition out of scope. Stage A (saml-smoke, 2026-09-27) found production accepting a locally signed response in all three positions and refusing a tampered signature with INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE : Failed to verify the signature in SAMLResponse; stage B (R2, owner-approved 2026-09-28) verifies signed responses in strict (crates/fireemu-adapter-http/src/saml.rs). Refusals rest on that observation and the public documentation (a missing signature or NameID); audience, destination, recipient, time windows, InResponseTo, issuer and the SHA-1 algorithms are not enforced until a record-saml recording observes them (list U1-U18).
NameID formats and the email of the ID token; the shape of firebase.sign_in_attributes, multi-valued attributes included. Subject to O5 as saml-response-verification.

Moved from AUTH-CREDENTIAL C7: the ID token of an IdP sign-in: firebase.identities, sign_in_provider and sign_in_attributes.

Moved from AUTH-CREDENTIAL C7: the claims of session cookies made from the original and the refreshed ID token. The cookie's auth_time is the sign-in's and its iat the cookie's: recorded relative to the cookie's iat, it is iat+0 or iat-1 by the second boundary (rehearsal, 2026-09-28) and may be lower in production, so the comparison accepts any auth_time <= iat on these rows instead of the exact value (pre-send review 2 of record-oidc).

Providers this parent does not sign in with (F3, F5): malformed and synthetic credentials for google.com and the other built-in providers, and their configuration. Strict refuses every built-in provider with INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE since O4 (3ed31eb80), unobserved; steps google-garbage-id-token and facebook-garbage-access-token observe production's answer to credentials it cannot verify. A genuine built-in credential cannot be observed (F3), so accepting one stays a known divergence: fireemu fetches no Google or Facebook key.
Every AUTH-FEDERATION row and the AUTH-ACCOUNT, AUTH-CREDENTIAL, AUTH-ACTION and AUTH-CONFIG-SDK regressions on one artifact, with the workspace tests and clippy.

An independent closure review and a safety review of the final artifact (no cargo-mutants in the reviews; the lane's own mutation evidence is checked). The safety review focuses on strict IdP verification (O4, 3ed31eb80): the signature check, key selection by kid, alg, the exp, iat, nbf, aud, azp, iss and nonce checks, the key size bounds, auth.idpSigners validation, the re-verification in the blocking-function commit and the continuation authority.
